title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Customer Comms
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s on-call and incident response standards: incident severity definitions, paging and escalation flows, runbook templates for common failure modes, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and handoffs, game day guidance, and customer/internal status page & comms templates. Use this as the canonical reference for responders, incident commanders (ICs), and comms leads.

Audience:
- On-call engineers (platform, serving runtime, infra)
- SRE and incident commanders
- Product and customer success teams drafting external comms

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction incident response flow that minimizes time-to-detect and time-to-repair while preserving accurate customer communications and blameless postmortems.
- Standardize runbooks for high-impact failure modes (service outage, tail latency, capacity exhaustion, downstream failures).
- Ensure clear ownership and fast escalation to avoid prolonged degradations.

1) Incident severity definitions
- SEV0 (Critical outage): Production API unavailable for >30% of requests or control plane unavailable. Customer-facing outages impacting SLAs. Page P0 escalation and executive alerts.
- SEV1 (Major): Significant degradation (high error rates >5% for 15+ minutes, or latency > 2x P50 SLO) impacting a subset of customers or routes. Page P1 and runbook.
- SEV2 (Minor): Noticeable reduction in quality (e.g., degraded model quality, transient errors <5%), non-blocking performance issues. Notify on-call, create incident ticket.
- SEV3 (Informational): Low-impact issues, investigations, or maintenance windows. Track as ops tasks.

2) Paging policy and escalation path
- Alerts originate from: Prometheus / Grafana alerts, PagerDuty integrations, Sentry, internal canaries, authoritative customer reports (support tickets).
- PagerDuty levels: P0 (SEV0), P1 (SEV1), P2 (SEV2). Team rotations are configured in PagerDuty with escalation to SRE lead after two minutes then to platform on-call after five minutes.
- Basic escalation flow:
  1. Initial page -> assigned on-call responder (ack within 2 minutes).
  2. If ack but unresolved after 10 minutes, escalate to on-call backup and notify team Slack channel #incidents.
  3. If no ack within 5 minutes, PagerDuty escalates to SRE lead and triggers an SMS.
  4. For SEV0, IC is appointed immediately by the first senior responder; notify CTO/VP Eng and Customer Success.

3) Roles & responsibilities (during an incident)
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates response, owns timeline and next actions, declares incident severity and timeline for updates.
- Primary Responder: Executes runbook steps and triage changes.
- Scribe/Note-taker: Documents timeline, commands, mitigation steps, and hypotheses in the incident doc (internal incident google doc).
- Comms Lead: Drafts status page and customer-facing messages; coordinates with CS and Legal if sensitive data involved.
- Ownership: IC assigns owners for mitigation, rollback, and postmortem.

4) Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm alert validity (check monitoring, recent deploys, config changes).
2. Identify scope: global vs region-specific; determine affected services and endpoints.
3. Gather symptoms: error rates, latency percentiles, logs, recent deploys, capacity events.
4. Appoint IC and scribe.
5. Post initial update to #incidents Slack channel with SEV, affected service(s), and initial ETA for next update.

5) Runbook templates (copy-and-run)
- Common runbook: Service outage (e.g., api-frontend/service-gateway)
  - Indicators: 5xx > 30% across region, healthcheck failures, influx of 503s.
  - Immediate steps:
    1. Verify alert (Grafana dashboard link, canary checks).
    2. Check recent deploys (CI/CD pipeline, git tag) in last 30 minutes: `ci get-deploys --service api-frontend --since 30m`
    3. Check pods/containers: `kubectl get pods -n production -l app=api-frontend`
    4. Inspect logs for repeated exceptions: `kubectl logs -n production -l app=api-frontend --since=10m | grep ERROR`
    5. If deployment related, roll back to last-known-good: `ci rollback --service api-frontend --to=stable`
    6. If resource exhaustion, scale replicas or cordon node and move traffic to healthy pool.
    7. When mitigation applied, validate by watching error-rate and canaries for 5 minutes.
  - Post-incident action items: root cause hypothesis, metric-driven validation, follow-up tasks (bug, monitoring improvements).

- Common runbook: Elevated tail latency for model-serving (kv-cache or batching problem)
  - Indicators: 95/99/99.9 pcts spike, request queue growth, GPU utilization low but CPU high on routing pods.
  - Immediate steps:
    1. Check model server logs and GPU process liveness.
    2. Verify KV cache hit rate metrics; if cache thrash detected, temporarily disable batching or reduce base batch size via runtime config: `redwood-config set --service serving --batches.max_size 8`
    3. If KV cache corruption suspected, restart serving nodes in rolling manner and monitor latency.
    4. If queuing persists, increase workers or redirect traffic to compatible lower-latency model variant.

Runbook best practices:
- Keep runbooks short (ideally under 20 steps) with exact CLI commands and dashboard links.
- Include rollback instructions and safe scaling steps.
- Each runbook must list owner, last_tested date, and link to runbook test results.

6) Postmortem requirements (blameless)
- Every SEV0/SEV1 incident requires a postmortem within 5 business days. SEV2 at discretion of IC.
- Postmortem template (must be filled in Confluence postmortems page):
  - Title, Incident ID, SEV, Date/time window
  - Summary (1-3 sentence customer-facing description)
  - Timeline (minute-granular, actions, and owners)
  - Root cause analysis (facts -> hypothesis -> validation)
  - Impact (customers affected, API downtime, SLA breaches, MTTD/MTTR numbers)
  - Mitigations applied during incident and long-term fixes planned
  - Action items with owners and due dates (JIRA links)
  - Lessons learned and monitoring/alerting changes
  - Severity reclassification notes (if any)
  - Postmortem reviewer sign-off (SRE lead and product owner)

7) On-call rotations & handoffs
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary rotations for platform and runtime teams, with a daily overlap/handoff window at 09:00 UTC for a 15-minute sync.
- Handoff checklist (outgoing -> incoming):
  1. Review open incidents and on-call tickets.
  2. Confirm any ongoing mitigations or escalations.
  3. Share recent deploys and changes in flight.
  4. Verify contact methods and escalation paths.
  5. Post a short handoff note to #oncall-handoffs Slack with key items.
- Backup policy: Each primary rotation has a 1-step backup assigned; if primary is unavailable, PagerDuty will escalate to the backup after 5 minutes.

8) Game days (scheduled incident drills)
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, alerting fidelity, and cross-team communications.
- Frequency: Quarterly for core platform services, biannually for lower-risk subsystems.
- Game day plan template:
  1. Objective & scope (service(s) in scope)
  2. Hypothesis to test (e.g., "Can we restore traffic within 10 minutes for a single-region outage?")
  3. Pre-game checklist (backup on-call, monitoring bookmarks, test playbooks, rollback keys)
  4. Execution steps and success criteria
  5. Post-game retro & action items (update runbooks, fix monitoring gaps)
- Game day ownership: platform SRE owns scheduling; respective service owners provide runbook authors and test participants.

9) Status page & customer communications templates
- Tools: StatusPage (external), internal status dashboard (Grafana), and #incidents Slack for internal updates.
- Update cadence: SEV0 — every 15 minutes until resolved; SEV1 — every 30 minutes until resolved; SEV2 — at least one update within 4 business hours.
- External status template (short):
  - Title: [Identified] Partial outage impacting /v1/generate (region: us-west-2)
  - Impact: Customers may see 503 or increased latency for text-generation requests.
  - Status: Investigating
  - Next update: in 15 minutes
  - Mitigation: Traffic has been partially rerouted to fallback region; we are investigating root cause.
- Internal Slack update template (detailed):
  - SEV: P0
  - IC: @avery.chen
  - Summary: Observed 30% 5xx on api-frontend beginning 10:12 UTC, affects us-west-2.
  - Current actions: Rolling back last deploy; scaling api-frontend replicas; validating canaries.
  - Next update: in 15 minutes or on significant change
- Customer support/email/CS template (suitable for CS to send):
  - Subject: Service disruption affecting text-generation in US-West
  - Body: We are aware of and actively investigating a disruption impacting text-generation requests in the US-West region. Engineers are actively diagnosing and we will provide updates every 15 minutes. We apologize for the impact and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

10) Metrics, SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for paid customers. Alert: immediately if availability drops below 99.9% for 10 minutes.
- Error rate alert: 5xx > 1% for 5 minutes -> P1, 5xx > 5% for 2 minutes -> P0.
- Latency alerts: P95 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes -> P1; P99 > 3x baseline -> P0.
- Canary failures: any canary failure for 3 consecutive checks -> P1.

11) Tools & integrations
- PagerDuty (paging, schedules)
- Slack channels: #incidents (incident coordination), #oncall-handoffs, #postmortems
- StatusPage (external customer updates)
- Grafana & Prometheus (monitoring and alerting)
- Sentry (error aggregation)
- Internal incident doc templates (link to Confluence incident docs repository)

12) Runbook maintenance & testing
- Ownership: each runbook must have an assigned owner (service owner) and a last_tested date field.
- Quarterly review: owners must validate runbooks via dry-run or game day at least once per quarter.
- Deprecated runbooks should be archived with a reason and replaced by new ones.

13) Quick reference: escalation contacts
- SRE lead (pager): @riley.morgan (PagerDuty escalation)
- Platform on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (link)
- Eng Manager on-call escalation: @priya.singh (sms)
- Customer Success escalation: @jordan.patel (email & Slack)

Appendix A — Example incident timeline (abridged)
- 10:12 UTC: Canary fails -> alert triggered (P0)
- 10:13 UTC: PagerDuty page acknowledged by on-call; IC established
- 10:15 UTC: Initial diagnosis: recent deploy to api-frontend
- 10:20 UTC: Rollback initiated to stable; traffic partially restored to canary nodes
- 10:35 UTC: Error rate dropped under threshold; begin validation
- 11:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; postmortem task created (JIRA-1234)

Appendix B — Post-incident action item example
- Title: Increase alert sensitivity for KV cache thrash
- Owner: @alex.kim
- Due: 2026-03-01
- Action: Add new alert for kv_cache.evictions > 1000/min and run game day to validate alert.

Contact & ownership
- Doc owner: Avery Chen (eng-sre) — please ping for doc updates or runbook additions.

If anything in this playbook conflicts with an on-call runbook for a specific service, the service runbook overrides this playbook for that service; however, the postmortem, communication cadence, and SEV definitions remain company-wide standards.
